nodes.label: orderideal.py — register 66 re-measured for R3
nodes.rationale: Runs the test register 66 states against the seated observed data, imports LW1-ground.py, offers no verdict, and files its measurement.

nodes.label: Register 66's order-ideal claim
nodes.rationale: The occupied cells form an order ideal of Lambda, downward closed without exception: 118 cells, 0 violations, 1 of 120 admissible l-orderings.

nodes.label: The counts differ before the property does
nodes.rationale: 118, 110 and 98 come from three element ranges; all three conventions agree the set is not downward closed, and two independently give 0 of 120 — a pure property of the occupied set that does not move with the range.

nodes.label: Occupancy gaps in five subshells
nodes.rationale: A subshell realised at some occupancy while a lower occupancy in the same subshell is realised by no element: 3d4, 3d9, 4d9 and 5d8 are forced by the anomalous configurations the seated member itself records.

nodes.label: LW1-ground.py — the observed ground configurations
nodes.rationale: Register 1306, NIST ASD 5.12, Z = 1..108, read not computed; its docstring records that every previous aufbau-plus-patch table was wrong at Pd.

nodes.label: Z is not a linear extension either
nodes.rationale: Six elements drop a subshell their predecessor held over Z = 1..108, against nine reported by the unbanked re-measurement — same direction, different count, consistent with different ranges.

nodes.label: The narrowed R3 question
nodes.rationale: Not whether register 66 is true, but which object it quantifies over and whether that object is the observed table; as printed it says ground-state configuration, which the seated member reads as the observed one.
